rounds.proof_sketch: The removed __syncthreads() creates a race condition where warp 0 could read warp_maxs[1..7] before other warps write. With 8 warps (256 threads, warp_id ∈ {0..7}), warp 0 reading stale data would corrupt final max. However, 112 rounds including structured stress patterns (tail_heavy, boundary_last_element) passed, indicating the race doesn't manifest on this GPU/driver combination due to hardware-level shared memory coherence.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes a __syncthreads() barrier between shared memory writes and reads across warps. While this is semantically a data race in CUDA's memory model, modern GPU implementations typically provide strong shared memory coherence within a threadblock. The warp scheduler often keeps warps relatively synchronized, and shared memory writes become visible quickly. Layer 2's 112 test rounds including adversarial patterns (tail_heavy placing max at end, boundary_last_element) failed to expose the race, suggesting the hardware provides stronger guarantees than CUDA formally specifies.
rounds.kill_strategy: This race condition is theoretically killable but practically unkillable under normal test conditions. The race would require specific warp scheduling where warp 0 reads shared memory before other warps' writes become visible. Modern GPUs' shared memory coherence and warp scheduling typically prevent this. No value-level input can reliably trigger hardware scheduling differences.
rounds.recommendations: When testing synchronization removal mutations, consider using CUDA's memory fence stress testing tools (cuda-memcheck with race detection, or compute-sanitizer). Pure differential testing cannot reliably expose races that depend on hardware scheduling. For critical code, document why synchronization is necessary and consider static analysis tools that detect race conditions.
